+"""Standalone copy of the bytecode stream writer from _pytest.assertion.rewrite."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import importlib.util
+import marshal
+import os
+import struct
+import types
+from typing import IO
+
+
+__all__ = ["vendored_pyc_stream", "vendored_pyc_stream_variant"]
+
+
+def vendored_pyc_stream(
+    fp: IO[bytes], source_stat: os.stat_result, co: types.CodeType
+) -> None:
+    # Technically, we don't have to have the same pyc format as
+    # (C)Python, since these "pycs" should never be seen by builtin
+    # import. However, there's little reason to deviate.
+    fp.write(importlib.util.MAGIC_NUMBER)
+    # https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0552/
+    flags = b"\x00\x00\x00\x00"
+    fp.write(flags)
+    # as of now, bytecode header expects 32-bit numbers for size and mtime (#4903)
+    mtime = int(source_stat.st_mtime) & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    size = source_stat.st_size & 0xFFFFFFFF
+    # "<LL" stands for 2 unsigned longs, little-endian.
+    fp.write(struct.pack("<LL", mtime, size))
+    fp.write(marshal.dumps(co))
+
+
+def vendored_pyc_stream_variant(
+    fp: IO[bytes], source_stat: os.stat_result, co: types.CodeType
+) -> None:
+    """Write bytecode to the stream and flush it on success."""
+    vendored_pyc_stream(fp, source_stat, co)
+    fp.flush()

@@ -0,0 +1,62 @@
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import importlib.util
+import io
+import marshal
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+
+class TestPycStream(unittest.TestCase):
+    writers = ("vendored_pyc_stream", "vendored_pyc_stream_variant")
+
+    def setUp(self) -> None:
+        path = (
+            Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "src/standalone_wave6_pyc_stream.py"
+        )
+        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("standalone_pyc_stream", path)
+        assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
+        self.module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+        spec.loader.exec_module(self.module)
+
+    def _check_write(
+        self, source: str, source_stat: os.stat_result, stat_header: bytes
+    ) -> None:
+        code = compile(source, "<test>", "exec")
+        header = importlib.util.MAGIC_NUMBER + bytes(4) + stat_header
+        for name in self.writers:
+            with self.subTest(writer=name):
+                output = io.BytesIO()
+                stream = mock.Mock(spec=output, wraps=output)
+                writer = getattr(self.module, name)
+                self.assertIsNone(writer(stream, source_stat, code))
+                self.assertEqual(output.getvalue(), header + marshal.dumps(code))
+                if name == "vendored_pyc_stream_variant":
+                    stream.flush.assert_called_once_with()
+                    self.assertEqual(stream.mock_calls[-1], mock.call.flush())
+                else:
+                    stream.flush.assert_not_called()
+
+    def test_write_masks_header_fields(self) -> None:
+        source_stat = os.stat_result((0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0x1_0000_0009, 0, -2.75, 0))
+        self._check_write("value = 7", source_stat, b"\xfe\xff\xff\xff\x09\x00\x00\x00")
+
+    def test_write_empty_source(self) -> None:
+        self._check_write("", os.stat_result((0,) * 10), bytes(8))
+
+    def test_write_error_does_not_flush(self) -> None:
+        source_stat = os.stat_result((0,) * 10)
+        code = compile("", "<test>", "exec")
+        for name in self.writers:
+            with self.subTest(writer=name):
+                writer = getattr(self.module, name)
+                error = OSError("write failed")
+                stream = mock.Mock(spec=io.BytesIO)
+                stream.write.side_effect = [4, 4, 8, error]
+                with self.assertRaises(OSError) as raised:
+                    writer(stream, source_stat, code)
+                self.assertIs(raised.exception, error)
+                self.assertEqual(stream.write.call_count, 4)
+                stream.flush.assert_not_called()
notes:
Copied the upstream writer body unchanged into a standard-library-only module and put the flush in a wrapper that runs it only after a successful write. File-path tests cover header masking, empty source, and write errors without requiring platform APIs.
